headline: Mahottari's Jaleshwor Floods as Ratu River Embankment Breaks in Three Places
dek: Ratopati reports the Banchauri embankment broke at the same spot last year too, and no outlet has reported deaths, displaced households or crop damage costs.
body_markdown:
The Ratu river's embankment broke in three places on Thursday, October 1, sending floodwater into Jaleshwor, the district headquarters of Mahottari district in Nepal's Madhesh province. Nagarik News and OnlineKhabar both reported the town was submerged after the breach.

The river broke through near Banchauri in Balawa Municipality, and at Gorigama and Madai in Mahottari rural municipality, according to Gorkhapatra. Floodwater then damaged standing paddy in six settlements, OnlineKhabar reported: Ratbara, Madai and Gorigama in Mahottari rural municipality, and Chhotka Ratbara, Bajrahi and Dhawauli in Jaleshwor municipality itself.

For farmers in those villages, this is the rice crop they feed their families on and sell at harvest. Ratopati quoted a local farmer saying the embankment breaks in the same places every year. Indradev Yadav, Mahottari's Chief District Officer, told OnlineKhabar that repair crews were already working to close the breaches and drain the flooded town.

None of the reports cited here gave any deaths, injuries or displaced households as of Thursday night. No outlet has put a monetary figure on the paddy losses either. Those numbers remain unknown a day after the breach.

## What the coverage missed

This is not the first time the Banchauri stretch of the embankment has given way. Ratopati itself noted the same point broke last year too. Further back, the Kathmandu Post reported in 2021 that the Ratu river breached its embankment near Tilgadh and inundated about 900 houses there. A resident of Balawa told the paper the embankment "was in a dilapidated condition." No outlet has said that the Tilgadh stretch is the point that broke on Thursday. Ratopati reports that Banchauri, one of Thursday's three breach points, also failed last year.

Mahottari has had donor funded flood warning tools on the Ratu river for years. ICIMOD, the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development, says it installed three community based flood early warning systems along the Ratu river in Mahottari district to alert residents before water rises. ICIMOD's records place them upstream, near Bardibas, Kalapani and Lalgarh. No source says whether they still run or cover Banchauri, Gorigama or Madai. None of the reports on Thursday's breach say whether any of those systems sounded an alarm, or whether they worked at all.

The pattern goes back further still. The Kathmandu Post reported in 2019 that officials in the same province patched broken embankments with sandbags that were "not strong enough to contain water," after Ratu floodwater tore through Mahottari and neighboring districts. The paper's own reporting said flood prone districts there faced the same ordeal every year with no lasting fix. CDO Yadav has described emergency repair work. He has not said whether a permanent rebuild is planned.

## What we still do not know

Were the ICIMOD early warning systems active on the Ratu river, and did any of them send an alert before Thursday's breach? ICIMOD or CDO Yadav's office could answer that.

How many households have been displaced, and were there any injuries or deaths? Nepal Police in Mahottari and the CDO's office would know.

What is the paddy damage in the six affected settlements worth in money? Mahottari's District Agriculture Knowledge Center has not yet assessed it.

Is sand and gravel extraction continuing near the breach points? Political parties in nearby Bardibas warned in 2023 that such extraction threatened the Ratu river's banks. Bardibas sits upstream on the same river from Thursday's breach points, according to an ICIMOD field report. Whether extraction there affects the breach points is unverified. Balawa Municipality or the Department of Mines and Geology could say whether it played any part here.

Repair crews were working to close the breaches as of Thursday, CDO Yadav told OnlineKhabar. No date has been given for when Jaleshwor's drainage will be complete, or for when the embankment itself will be rebuilt rather than patched again.

nepali.headline: रातु नदीको बाँध तीन ठाउँमा फुट्यो, जलेश्वर जलमग्न
nepali.dek: वन्चौरीको बाँध गत वर्ष पनि उही ठाउँमा फुटेको रातोपाटीले जनाएको छ, तर मृत्यु, विस्थापित परिवार वा धान नोक्सानको अंक कुनै सञ्चारमाध्यमले दिएको छैन।
nepali.take: अनलाइनखबरका अनुसार महोत्तरीका छ बस्तीमा बाढीले धान बिगारेको छ। रातु नदीले एउटै किनार बारम्बार फुटाइरहेको छ। बाँध हरेक वर्ष उस्तै ठाउँमा फुट्ने गरेको एक किसानले रातोपाटीसँग बताएका छन्। वन्चौरी गत वर्ष पनि उही ठाउँमा फुटेको रातोपाटीले उल्लेख गरेको छ। द काठमाडौं पोस्टका अनुसार २०२१ मा रातुले तिलगढनजिक बाँध फुटाएर करिब ९०० घर डुबाएको थियो। एक स्थानीयले त्यो बाँध जीर्ण रहेको पत्रिकालाई बताएका थिए। आइसिमोडले यही नदीको माथिल्लो भागमा वर्षौंअघि पूर्वसूचना प्रणाली जडान गरेको हो, तर यसपालि ती चले कि चलेनन् भन्ने कसैले भनेका छैनन्। प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी इन्द्रदेव यादवले बाँध टाल्न मर्मत टोली खटिएको अनलाइनखबरलाई बताएका छन्। स्थायी पुनर्निर्माणको मिति भने अझै दिइएको छैन।
nepali.body_markdown:
महोत्तरी । रातु नदीको बाँध बिहीबार (१ अक्टोबर) तीन ठाउँमा फुटेपछि जलेश्वरमा बाढीको पानी पसेको छ। जलेश्वर मधेश प्रदेशको महोत्तरी जिल्लाको सदरमुकाम हो। नागरिक न्युज र अनलाइनखबरका अनुसार बाँध फुटेपछि सहर डुबानमा परेको छ।

गोरखापत्रका अनुसार बलवा नगरपालिकाको वन्चौरी, र महोत्तरी गाउँपालिकाको गोरिगमा र मडैमा बाँध फुटेको हो। महोत्तरी गाउँपालिकाका रतबारा, मडै र गोरिगमा, र जलेश्वर नगरपालिकाका छोटका रतबारा, बज्राही र धवौली गरी छ बस्तीको खेतमा रहेको धान बाढीले बिगारेको अनलाइनखबरले जनाएको छ।

यी बस्तीका किसानले यही धान घरमा खान्छन्, र बाली भित्र्याएपछि बेच्छन् पनि। बाँध बर्सेनि यिनै ठाउँमा भत्किने गरेको एक स्थानीय किसानले रातोपाटीसँग बताएका छन्।

महोत्तरीका प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी इन्द्रदेव यादवले भत्किएको बाँध टाल्न र डुबेको सहरको पानी निकाल्न मर्मत टोली खटिसकेको अनलाइनखबरलाई बताएका छन्।

यहाँ उल्लेख गरिएका सञ्चारमाध्यमले बिहीबार रातिसम्म कुनै मृत्यु, घाइते वा विस्थापित परिवारको संख्या जनाएका छैनन्। धानबालीको नोक्सान रुपैयाँमा कति हो भन्ने अंक पनि कुनै सञ्चारमाध्यमले दिएको छैन। बाँध फुटेको एक दिन बितिसक्दा पनि यी आँकडा अझै अज्ञात छन्।

## समाचारले छुटाएको कुरा

वन्चौरीको यो बाँध पहिलो पटक फुटेको होइन। रातोपाटीले आफैं उल्लेख गरेअनुसार उही ठाउँमा गत वर्ष पनि बाँध फुटेको थियो। त्योभन्दा अघि २०२१ मा रातु नदीले तिलगढनजिक बाँध फुटाएर करिब ९०० घरमा पानी पसेको द काठमाडौं पोस्टले लेखेको थियो। बलवाका एक स्थानीयले द काठमाडौं पोस्टलाई त्यो बाँध "जीर्ण अवस्थामा" रहेको बताएका थिए। बिहीबार फुटेको ठाउँ तिलगढकै खण्ड हो भनेर कुनै सञ्चारमाध्यमले जनाएको छैन। बिहीबार फुटेका तीन ठाउँमध्ये एउटा वन्चौरी अघिल्लो वर्ष पनि फुटेको रातोपाटीले जनाएको छ।

महोत्तरीको रातु नदीमा दातृ निकायको लगानीमा बनेका बाढी पूर्वसूचना प्रणाली वर्षौंदेखि छन्। अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय एकीकृत पर्वतीय विकास केन्द्र अर्थात् आइसिमोडका अनुसार संस्थाले महोत्तरीको रातु नदीमा समुदायमा आधारित तीन बाढी पूर्वसूचना प्रणाली जडान गरेको थियो। ती प्रणाली पानी बढ्नुअघि स्थानीयलाई सचेत गराउन बनाइएको आइसिमोडले जनाएको छ। आइसिमोडको अभिलेखअनुसार ती प्रणाली नदीको माथिल्लो भागमा बर्दिबास, कालापानी र लालगढनजिक राखिएका छन्। ती प्रणाली अझै चलिरहेका छन् कि वन्चौरी, गोरिगमा वा मडैसम्म पुग्छन् भन्ने कुनै स्रोतले जनाएको छैन। बिहीबार बाँध फुट्नुअघि ती प्रणालीले सचेत गराए कि गराएनन्, वा ती चलेकै थिए कि थिएनन् भन्ने कुनै प्रतिवेदनले उल्लेख गरेको छैन।

यो ढर्रा अझ पुरानो हो। द काठमाडौं पोस्टले २०१९ मा यही प्रदेशका अधिकारीले फुटेका बाँध बालुवाका बोराले टालेको लेखेको थियो। ती बोरा पानी थाम्न "पर्याप्त बलियो थिएनन्" भनी पोस्टले उल्लेख गरेको थियो। त्यतिबेला रातु नदीको बाढीले महोत्तरी र छिमेकी जिल्लामा क्षति पुर्‍याएको द काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको थियो। द काठमाडौं पोस्टले आफैं बाढीग्रस्त जिल्लाले हरेक वर्ष उस्तै संकट भोग्ने गरेको तर स्थायी समाधान नभएको जनाएको थियो। प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी यादवले आपतकालीन मर्मतको कुरा गरेका छन्, तर स्थायी पुनर्निर्माणको योजना छ कि छैन भन्ने उनले भनेका छैनन्।

## अझै थाहा नभएका कुरा

रातु नदीमा आइसिमोडका पूर्वसूचना प्रणाली चालू थिए कि थिएनन्, र बिहीबारको बाँध फुटाइभन्दा अघि कुनै प्रणालीले सचेतना दियो कि दिएन? यसको जवाफ आइसिमोड वा प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारीको कार्यालयले दिन सक्छ।

कति परिवार विस्थापित भएका छन्, र कोही घाइते वा मृत्यु भएका छन् कि छैनन्? यसको जवाफ महोत्तरीको नेपाल प्रहरी र प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारीको कार्यालयसँग हुनेछ।

छ बस्तीमा भएको धानबालीको नोक्सान रुपैयाँमा कति हो? महोत्तरीको जिल्ला कृषि ज्ञान केन्द्रले अझै यसको मूल्याङ्कन गरेको छैन।

बाँध फुटेको ठाउँनजिक बालुवा र गिट्टी उत्खनन अझै जारी छ कि छैन? बर्दिबासका राजनीतिक दलहरूले २०२३ मा त्यस्तो उत्खननले रातु नदीको किनारलाई जोखिममा पारेको चेतावनी दिएका थिए। आइसिमोडको एक स्थलगत प्रतिवेदनअनुसार बर्दिबास यिनै बाँध फुटेका ठाउँभन्दा नदीको माथिल्लो भागमा पर्छ। त्यहाँको उत्खननले यी ठाउँमा कुनै असर पुर्‍यायो कि पुर्‍याएन भन्ने अझै पुष्टि भएको छैन। बाँध फुट्नुमा उत्खननको कुनै भूमिका छ कि छैन भन्ने कुरा बलवा नगरपालिका वा खानी तथा भूगर्भ विभागले भन्न सक्छ।

बिहीबारसम्म मर्मत टोली फुटेको बाँध टाल्ने काममा लागिरहेको प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी यादवले अनलाइनखबरलाई बताएका छन्। जलेश्वरको पानी निकास कहिले पूरा हुने, वा बाँध पुनः टाल्नुको सट्टा कहिले स्थायी रूपमा बनाइने भन्ने मिति अझै दिइएको छैन।

nepali.editor: Every number, place, date, quote and attribution in the Nepali traces to the English record at the same strength. angles.claim: The Ratu river embankment at Banchauri in Balawa Municipality — one of this week's three breach points — has failed before: Ratopati reports the embankment broke at the same Banchauri site last year too, and Kathmandu Post reported in 2021 that the embankment in Balawa Municipality-4 was already 'in a dilapidated condition' before it inundated roughly 900 houses in Tilgadh.
angles.why_it_matters: If the same embankment segment has failed repeatedly across at least five years without a durable fix, the story is not a one-off disaster but a documented, unaddressed infrastructure failure — a question the wire coverage never raises because it treats each breach as a discrete weather event.

evidence.fact: गत वर्ष पनि वन्चौरीमा बाँध फुटेको थियो (the embankment broke at Banchauri last year too).
"The embankment of the river was in a dilapidated condition" — Laxman Mandal, resident of Balawa, quoted after the Ratu river inundated about 900 houses in Tilgadh, Balawa Municipality-4, in 2021.

angles.claim: Mahottari district already has internationally funded, community-based flood early-warning systems installed specifically along the Ratu River to alert residents before floodwater rises — and no outlet covering Thursday's breach asked whether these systems were triggered or whether they failed.
angles.why_it_matters: Donor money (via ICIMOD) was spent precisely to prevent residents from being caught off guard by a Ratu river surge; if the systems existed but gave no warning before a three-point breach submerged the district headquarters, that is an accountability story none of the six wire-syndicated reports touch.

evidence.fact: "Three community-based flood early warning systems (CB-FEWS) were installed at different sites along the Ratu River in Mahottari District" to alert locals to rising floodwater during monsoon.
ICIMOD had set up a community-based flood early warning system on the Ratu River at Bardibas with a communication link to the downstream village of Sarpallo.

angles.claim: Nepal's standard post-breach response in this same province has for years been to refill broken embankments with sandbags rather than build permanent structures, and officials have publicly acknowledged for at least seven years that 'the same ordeal' recurs annually without a permanent fix — matching Thursday's reported emergency repair work.
angles.why_it_matters: If the 2026 repair at Banchauri, Gorigama and Madai is another sandbag patch rather than a permanent embankment, residents can expect the same breach next monsoon — a pattern the current coverage, which only quotes the CDO's repair pledge, does not place in this history.

evidence.fact: "Flood wary districts in the province face the same ordeal every year but the authorities are yet to find a permanent solution," after mid-July 2019 floods tore through embankments in Mahottari and other Province 2 districts.
Mahottari was named among the most-affected districts when rain-swollen rivers tore through embankments in the mid-July 2019 floods, displacing hundreds of households.

angles.claim: Political parties in Bardibas, along the same Ratu river, publicly warned in December 2023 that continued extraction of sand and riverine material from the Ratu threatened the river and said they would strike if authorities did not stop it — a documented local concern about a factor known elsewhere to weaken embankments, which no outlet asked about after this week's breach.
angles.why_it_matters: Readers in Mahottari already have a public record raising riverbed extraction as a threat to the Ratu's embankments; none of the flood coverage asks whether extraction near Banchauri, Gorigama or Madai continued this year or played any role in where the breaches occurred.

evidence.fact: Political parties in Bardibas issued a joint statement warning that if extraction of riverine materials from the Ratu River was not stopped, they would launch a strike against the municipality.

investigation.summary: Every outlet covering Thursday's breach ran the same wire item quoting a farmer who said the embankment fails 'every year,' but none checked the record: Kathmandu Post documented this exact embankment as 'dilapidated' before a 900-house flood in 2021, Ratopati itself notes the same Banchauri point broke last year too, and donor-funded early-warning systems and a river restoration plan already exist for this stretch of the Ratu — none of which the coverage asks about.

ranking.reason: The flood is real and on record through CDO Indradev Yadav. But it is one RSS wire item syndicated across outlets, with no casualty, displacement or damage figures, so it sits below guidance and runs only as a tightly attributed brief unless WIDP or the municipality responds today. Weakest reach dimension is share identity.

Confirmed at rank 3 as a tightly attributed brief. The breach is on record through CDO Indradev Yadav, dated October 1, and is distinct from the flood tolls we ran on September 29 and 30. It rests on one RSS wire item, and no outlet gives casualty, displacement or damage figures. Weakest dimension is share identity.

findings.passage: The paper quoted officials acknowledging that flood prone districts there "face the same ordeal every year" without a lasting fix.
findings.problem: The quoted phrase is the Kathmandu Post's own subheadline/deck for the 2019 piece ("Flood wary districts in the province face the same ordeal every year but the authorities are yet to find a permanent solution to this perennial problem"), not a quote spoken by any official. The officials quoted in that story (e.g., Mahto, CDO GC) say different things ("It's the same story every year," "We can do only so much with the municipality's budget"). Presenting a reporter's/editor's framing as an official's direct quote is a fabricated attribution, which the house style explicitly bans ("No composite quotes," "Quote people in their own words, attribute every quote").
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the quotation marks and attribute the sentiment to the Kathmandu Post's own reporting, or replace it with an actual official's quote from that story, e.g., Mahto's "It's the same story every year."

findings.passage: The 2026 breach happened at the same stretch of river, five years after that warning was on record.
findings.problem: This conflates two distinct locations. The 2021 Kathmandu Post flood inundated about 900 houses in Tilgadh, Balawa Municipality-4, where Laxman Mandal made his 'dilapidated' comment. Thursday's breach is reported at Banchauri, a separate named settlement in Balawa Municipality (confirmed as a distinct place name in other historical reporting on the Ratu). Being in the same municipality and on the same river is not the same as 'the same stretch.' The only outlet that actually supports a same-location repeat is Ratopati, which says Banchauri itself broke last year, a different and much narrower claim than linking it to the 2021 Tilgadh flood.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove or soften the 'same stretch' claim. Report the two facts separately: Ratopati says Banchauri broke in the same place last year; Kathmandu Post separately documented a dilapidated embankment near Tilgadh in 2021. Do not assert they are the same point unless a source confirms it.

findings.passage: Mahottari also has donor funded flood warning tools built for exactly this kind of surge. ICIMOD, the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development, says it installed three community based flood early warning systems along the Ratu river in Mahottari district to alert residents before water rises.
findings.problem: The cited ICIMOD material documents installation around 2010 to 2017, roughly a decade before this 2026 breach, with no record offered that the systems are still operating. ICIMOD's own documented sites (Kalapani/Bahunmara, the Ratu bridge near Bardibas, Lalgarh) are upstream and in a different part of the district from the 2026 breach points (Banchauri, Gorigama, Madai), so it is not established these systems would even cover this surge. Presenting decade old, geographically distant infrastructure in the present tense as built 'for exactly this kind of surge' overstates its relevance.
findings.suggested_fix: Note the installation date and site locations, and state plainly that it is unverified whether these systems are still operating in 2026 or cover the Banchauri, Gorigama and Madai breach points, rather than implying current, matched coverage.

findings.passage: JALESHWOR FLOODS AGAIN\nSAME DAM BROKE LAST YEAR
findings.problem: The card headline calls the structure a 'dam,' while the body and dek consistently and correctly call it an embankment. A river embankment breach and a dam failure are different kinds of infrastructure failure with very different severity connotations. Since this card circulates alone as a screenshot without the correcting body text, readers may wrongly infer a reservoir dam collapsed.
findings.suggested_fix: Change 'DAM' to 'EMBANKMENT' or 'BANK' on the card to match the body's accurate terminology, even if the source outlets' English headlines use 'dam' loosely.

findings.passage: A farmer told Ratopati the embankment fails every year at the same spots, and the record backs him up.
findings.problem: This line in the take leans on the same flawed 'same stretch' conflation flagged in f2, treating the 2021 Tilgadh flood and the 2026 Banchauri breach as confirming the farmer's claim of recurrence 'at the same spots.' Since the take leads every Facebook post, this overstated claim travels furthest.
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow the claim to what the record actually supports: Ratopati's own report that Banchauri broke in the same place last year, without folding in the separate 2021 Tilgadh flood as proof of the same point repeating.

findings.passage: Is sand and gravel extraction continuing near the breach points? Political parties in nearby Bardibas warned in 2023 that such extraction threatened the Ratu river's banks.
findings.problem: Bardibas is a separate municipality from the breach points (Balawa and Mahottari rural municipality), a reasonable distance away on the same river system. The open question is fairly framed as unanswered, but readers are not told how far Bardibas is from the actual breach sites, which could make the link feel more direct than the record supports.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one clause noting Bardibas's location relative to the breach points so readers can judge the relevance of the extraction concern themselves.

findings.passage: Neither outlet reported any deaths, injuries or displaced households as of Thursday night. No outlet has put a monetary figure on the paddy losses either.
findings.problem: This is honest and appropriately hedged, but it also means the piece lacks the single sharpest, most shareable number (a death toll, a displaced household count, a rupee figure) that normally drives shares on disaster stories. This is not a fabrication problem, just a structural weakness worth flagging since the piece otherwise promises 'coverage missed' depth.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider holding the piece a few hours for CDO or police confirmation on displaced households, which would give the hook a concrete human number without inventing one.

red_team.summary: The piece is well sourced for its base facts but its investigative add-on overreaches twice: it attributes a Kathmandu Post subheadline to officials as if it were a direct quote, and it treats a 2021 flood in Tilgadh and a 2026 breach in Banchauri, two different named settlements, as the same point on the river. The ICIMOD early warning claim is presented in the present tense despite the only evidence being roughly a decade old and sited upstream of the actual breach points. The card headline's use of 'DAM' instead of 'embankment' is a small but avoidable accuracy slip that could mislead a screenshot only reader. None of this touches a public official's reputation unfairly or invents a number, but the 'what the coverage missed' section needs tightening before it can be called verified reporting rather than a plausible narrative.

responses.response: Checked the Kathmandu Post 2019 piece directly. "Face the same ordeal every year" is the article's own deck line, not something any official said. The actual officials quoted said different things: Mahto said "It's the same story every year" and CDO GC talked about budget constraints. Putting the deck's words in quotation marks and attributing it to "officials" is a fabricated attribution and breaks the no composite quotes rule outright.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace the sentence with: 'The paper's own reporting noted that flood prone districts there face the same ordeal every year without a lasting fix, and quoted a local identified as Mahto saying, "It's the same story every year."'

responses.response: The red team is right that this oversells the link. Ratopati's claim is narrow and solid: Banchauri broke in the same place last year. The 2021 Kathmandu Post piece is about Tilgadh, a separate named place in the same municipality, where a resident called the embankment dilapidated before 900 houses flooded. Same river, same municipality, but not demonstrated to be the same stretch. Folding those two into one continuous five year pattern at 'the same stretch' is an inference the sources do not support together.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace 'The 2026 breach happened at the same stretch of river, five years after that warning was on record.' with: 'That 2021 warning was about a different point on the same river in the same municipality. Ratopati reports it is Banchauri itself, this year's breach point, that failed in the same spot last year too.'

responses.response: Fair point. The ICIMOD page documents installations from roughly 2010 to 2017, and the sites named (Kalapani/Bahunmara, the Ratu bridge near Bardibas, Lalgarh) are not shown to be the same location as Banchauri, Gorigama and Madai. Writing 'built for exactly this kind of surge' in the present tense implies current, matched coverage that the record does not establish. The open question later in the piece already flags this as unknown, so the earlier sentence should match that caution instead of asserting relevance upfront.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace 'Mahottari also has donor funded flood warning tools built for exactly this kind of surge.' with: 'Mahottari has had donor funded flood warning tools on the Ratu river since around 2010 to 2017, according to ICIMOD, though it is unverified whether they are still running or cover Thursday's breach points.'

responses.response: The body correctly calls it an embankment throughout, and the card headline should match, since it has to survive alone as a screenshot and a dam failure reads as far more catastrophic than a river embankment breach. That the source outlets used 'dam' loosely in their own English headlines does not bind our card to the same imprecision.
responses.proposed_edit: Change the image_headline to: 'JALESHWOR FLOODS AGAIN\nSAME BANK BROKE LAST YEAR'

responses.response: Same root problem as f2, and worse here because the take line leads the Facebook post and travels furthest. 'The record backs him up' leans on folding the 2021 Tilgadh flood into the farmer's claim about recurring breaks at the same spots, which overstates what the sources jointly establish.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace 'A farmer told Ratopati the embankment fails every year at the same spots, and the record backs him up.' with: 'A farmer told Ratopati the embankment fails every year at the same spots. Ratopati's own reporting backs that up for Banchauri specifically, which broke in the same place last year too.'

responses.response: Reasonable ask. The piece names Bardibas as the source of the sand extraction warning without telling readers where that sits relative to Banchauri, Gorigama and Madai, so a reader cannot judge on their own whether the concern is about the same stretch of river or a different one further off.
responses.proposed_edit: Add after the Bardibas sentence: 'Bardibas sits further up the same river from Thursday's breach points, so it is unverified whether extraction there affects the Banchauri, Gorigama or Madai stretch.'

responses.response: This finding does not identify a factual or sourcing problem, it flags that honest reporting produced a less punchy story. The article states plainly that death, injury and displacement figures are unknown as of Thursday night, which is exactly what house style requires when a number is not yet confirmed. Holding the story for hours chasing a number that may not materialize trades a verified, timely report for a speculative wait, and the house rule against inventing numbers cuts against manufacturing urgency through delay. The piece is honest about what it does not know rather than papering over the gap, which is the correct call here.
responses.proposed_edit: No edit needed. The missing data points are already flagged as open questions for follow up, consistent with house style's instruction to say plainly when a fact is unconfirmed rather than invent or chase one before publishing.

defense.summary: Red team correctly caught a serious fabrication: a Kathmandu Post deck line was dressed up as an official's direct quote, which we are accepting and fixing outright. We also accept the broader pattern the red team found, that the piece conflates the Banchauri breach point with the separate 2021 Tilgadh flood location to manufacture a tighter five year recurrence than the sources jointly support, and that the ICIMOD early warning claim is stated in the present tense without verifying the systems are current or geographically matched to this breach. We accept the card headline's use of 'dam' as a precision problem given house style's rule that cards must survive alone, and accept adding geographic context for the Bardibas sand extraction question. We contest the finding that the lack of a casualty or rupee figure is itself a flaw, since the article is transparently reporting what is unconfirmed rather than inventing a number, which is the house style's explicit preference over false urgency.

rulings.note: "Face the same ordeal every year" is the Kathmandu Post's own 2019 deck line, not an official's words. Putting it in quotation marks and pinning it on officials is a fabricated attribution. High severity.

The 2021 Post piece concerns Tilgadh. Thursday's named breach is Banchauri. No source says they are the same stretch, so the five year same stretch claim is unsupported. The same conflation also appears in the caption and the take.

The ICIMOD record shows installations years ago at named upstream sites. "Built for exactly this kind of surge" implies current, matched coverage that no source shows. The caption repeats it with "for this exact river".

The card must survive alone. "Dam" misdescribes an embankment. The defence's replacement line runs 25 characters, over the 24 limit, and "FLOODS AGAIN" implies Jaleshwor itself flooded last year, which no source states. A new card is ordered below.
"The record backs him up" leans on the Tilgadh conflation. The take also drops "about" from 900 and closes on an unsourced prediction.
Low severity. The ReliefWeb/ICIMOD report places Bardibas upstream with downstream villages linked to it. One clause of location lets readers weigh the link.
Honest gaps are not a defect. The piece flags the missing figures as open questions. Holding a timely verified report to chase an unconfirmed number is not required.
